findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

During the inspection all of the sanitizer buckets were observed to not register quaternary ammonia sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. These buckets were observed changed during the inspection and prior to observation. The inspector then checked the dispenser in the kitchen and did not find evidence of the dispenser correctly dispensing sanitizer on either their test strips or the facility test strips. The PIC was consulted at that point and more investigation conducted. The buckets were remade manually with the concentrate and a call will be put in to the company contracted to manage the dispenser (EcoLab) and maintenance will need to be conducted moving forward.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. 

The dispenser used for sanitizers in the facility was not producing sanitizer at effective concentrations for sanitizing food contact surfaces. A temporary fix was put into place until EcoLab could be contacted and conduct maintenance. A ten day follow-up is being scheduled to allow for this maintenance to be completed.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

Multiple shelves above the three part sink have the paint worn away and chipping. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and re-seal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces subject to moisture are smooth and easily cleanable at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Heavy ice accumulation is observed in the walk in freezer. Previously this violation was noted as on the floor only and now includes major frost accumulation around the unit and ceiling of the freezer. The PIC is instructed to clean/defrost the area regularly to ensure an accumulation does not develop again. It is also suggested to have a professional examine the equipment and see if there is an external reason for the accumulation to develop.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival the sani buckets were all registering low on the inspector’s test strips. The buckets were remade during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

The thermometer in the reach in cooler next to the drive thru window has mold accumulation along the seams and back surface. Clean and maintain clean moving forward.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Multiple wiping rags used for cleaning spills off the counters are observed moist and sitting on the counters in the service area. Both flat sani buckets are also observed with heavily soiled solutions. The PIC was consulted, buckets remade with clean solution and the rags placed in solution to correct today’s violations.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

During this inspection the PIC was not aware of any equipment in the facility intended for ensuring that the temperature based dish machine reaches the critical temperature of 160F. Strips and dots that change color at 160 were discussed as well as a thermometer intended for measuring dish machines. Ensure that a measuring system is in place prior to the follow up in two weeks.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The bottom of the walk in freezer is coated with ice during this inspection. The PIC was consulted and instructed to remove the ice often enough to ensure that effective cleaning takes place.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The baffles and internal roof of the ice machine have an accumulation of potential molds built up on their surfaces. A conversation took place with the PIC and they’re instructed to clean these surfaces often enough to maintain them clean. The items were cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Accumulation of soil observed under espresso machines and other counter equipment. Clean frequently enough to prevent soil accumulation. Follow up at next routine inspection.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No certified food manager (CFM) present during the inspection. Medium risk facilities must have a CFM present at all times of food prep and service.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12 (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. (C)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed egg sandwiches on the left side/top shelf of the food under-counter cooler to be 55F (probed). Items were placed in this cooler at 12PM. Discussed Time as a Public Health Control and the 6 hour time limit on food stored below 70F. CORRECTED- PIC will check temperatures in 1 hour, if still out of temperature, items will be disposed of. Cooler thermometer was relocated to the warmer side of the cooler to aid in temperature monitoring.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 (A)(2) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained at 5ºC (41ºF) or less. (P)

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed multiple occurences where personal drinks or food were above service food. Ensure that personal items have a designated place within the facility and are kept in this area to prevent cross contamination. All items were moved during the inspection. 
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment:
Observed multiple issues with hot water throughout the facility. Shift manager states that he noticed recently that the water at particular sinks was not reaching proper temperatures. They've also had recent work done to remove hot water from particular rinse sinks in the operation. All hand sinks were without hot water (89F was greatest temperature when probed between 4 hand sinks). The three compartment sink reached 110-115F. The dish machine has an additional heat booster though that allowed it to reach the proper temperatures. There was mention of an incident in which the water heater was turned down due to a complaint that the water would burn people. The managers were not entirely sure as to if this incident truly occurred. Facility was told to contact a Plumber ASAP to make the needed repairs. If the water heater was adjusted by an employee, then this is not proper. The water heater is set by the plumber to ensure that it holds up to plumbing codes. If any further water issues occur within the facility, then a plumber should be contacted immediately. It would also be appreciated if SCDPH was made aware of such issues. Kevin Dreesman, Foods Supervisor for SCDPH, will be conducting a follow up inspection on the facility within the next 24 hours. He should be contacted as soon as the repairs have been made. See General Comments for Work Phone number.
750-1120 Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of coffee mix being stored on the floor by the back door. Ensure that food products are stored at least 6 inches off the floor. Also, observed a container of cool lime without a lid to the container. Ensure that food products are properly protected during storage. 
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed floors in the back corner dry storage to be soiled with coffee beans and other debris. Also, observed the drain below the three compartment sink to be soiled. Ensure that floors are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean condition.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed multiple articles (purses, coats, and other personal belongings) being stored on top of boxes of coffee mixes. Ensure that there is proper storage allocated for employee's personal belongings. Items were moved during the inspection. 
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
Observed that the duct tape that holds the weight onto the drain hose from the coffee machine is still in place. 
Remove the tape from the drain hose.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
Observed that the damp mop was not hung up between uses. 
Store mop hanging upright between uses to promote air drying.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed two boxes of single-service paper cups stored on the floor next to the 3 compartment sink.
750-880a Single service items shall be properly stored at least 6" off the floor.
Store single service items properly.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed That the floors in the following areas are soiled: 1) under the ice machine has some debris, 2) under the storage shelves in storage area there is some dust, 3) the floor drain under the 3 compartment sink has some build up.  
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.
Clean the floors in the above areas.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The inside surfaces of the oven have some baked-on food debris.  Clean and maintain this non-food contact surface.
750-800e.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Food debris/crumbs were found in the following clean utensil containers:  (A) tongs spot to the right of the oven, (B) forks container to the right of the oven.  Clean and maintain these clean utensil storage locations.          750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The following floors are soiled:  (A) walk-in freezer, (B) under right-side (upon entering) of walk-in cooler (milk splash), (C) under dish machine (in far corner), (D) floor drain under three-pan sink, (E) under side station of front counter (where counter top oven is located).  Clean and maintain these floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Container of white pellets found on floor by back door.  Staff state these are salt pellets for the water softener.  IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED - before inspection ended, this salt was added to water system.  
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: Currently, there is no full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager.  It appears one of the manager has completed a class on March 11, 2013, passed the examination early April, and is attempting to complete certification.  Complete certification for her and/or have another staff member certify.  Paperwork should be submitted this week.  IDPH FSSMC certificate Request  Form left with manager.          750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.comment:
Food debris and food wrapper found on floor of walk-in freezer.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
